_comment: Router registry per spec §3. `detection: 'to_address'` matches the tx's to field against the address. `detection: 'solver_eoa'` (not yet implemented) requires event-based detection — flag any router whose Basescan check shows an EOA instead of a contract. All addresses below verified as deployed contracts via eth_getCode against Base mainnet.
_removed_fee_recipients: The spec's §3 schema includes a per-router `fee_recipients` array. It was never populated and was REMOVED 2026-07-28 — don't re-add it. Fee sinks are detected from the trace instead: addresses that retain value are collected per trade, aggFeeBps is split across them proportionally to retained value, and each sink is labelled with its verified contract name.

routers.name: OKX
routers._verified: Verified on-chain 2026-07-15. Sourced from Basescan's project directory (basescan.org/directory/detail/68), labeled 'OKX: Dex Router 2'; getsourcecode confirms verified contract 'DexRouter' (24378 bytes, not a proxy). Live: 21210 logs / 5388 distinct txs in ~9000 blocks (~26k/day), the right order for DefiLlama's $11.9M/day. Emits OrderRecord 5445x over those 5388 txs (~1/tx). Sampled 40 recent OrderRecord txs: 31 had `to` == this router; the other 9 arrived via per-user EIP-1167 TradingVaultImplementation clones (0xbb07f41a…, 0xeedbb45f…) — smart accounts, not aggregators, and out of reach of to_address by design.

routers.name: OKX
routers._verified: IDENTITY verified, LIVENESS not. Basescan directory labels it 'OKX: DEX Router (ExactOut)'; getsourcecode confirms verified contract 'DexRouterExactOut' (14314 bytes). But it emitted ZERO logs in ~9000 blocks, so unlike every other entry here its settlement event is unconfirmed — no sample existed to observe. Kept active because identity is solid and `to` is what labels: a trade here is an OKX trade. If it wakes up, expect a correct OKX label; SETTLEMENT_EVENT_SEEN depends on it emitting OrderRecord like DexRouter, which is an assumption, not an observation.
